content: Lower respiratory tract infections are often equated with pneumonia, but this term also encompasses other infections such as lung abscesses, acute bronchitis, and emphysema. Lower respiratory tract infections are recognized as the leading cause of death among all infectious diseases. Acute bronchitis alone affects more than 40 adults per 1,000 individuals annually. Since 1993, there has been a slight decline in the overall number of deaths attributed to lower respiratory tract infections. However, in 2002, these infections remained the primary cause of death from infectious diseases, responsible for 3.9 million deaths globally, accounting for 6.9% of all deaths that year. A variety of acute and chronic infections can impact the lower respiratory tract. While antibiotics are frequently considered the first-line treatment for these infections, they are not effective against viral infections. It is critical to select antibiotics based on the specific causative organism and to adapt treatment strategies in response to the evolving nature of these infections and the increasing resistance to standard therapies. Lower respiratory tract infections impose a significant financial burden on healthcare systems and are generally more severe than infections of the upper respiratory tract.
